title: The Honey Hall
text: An old hall gone to the bees, its windows blind with comb, honey dripping in slow gold ropes from the rafters. The air hums. The bees are huge, as big as sparrows, slow and furred and very curious about you.

options.label: Gather honey from the rafters, and hope the bees are feeling generous.

outcomes.text: The bees allow it, this once, humming around your heads.
The bees do not allow it, and there are a great many bees.

options.label: The cleverest smokes them out first, before anyone reaches for the comb.

outcomes.text: Sleepy bees, slow as falling leaves, and a great deal of honey.

options.label: Leave them to their hall. It is theirs now.

outcomes.text: They follow you to the door, humming. One stings the Leader, gently, almost fondly, and the arm swells stiff.
